articles.summary: A baby fever is a rectal temperature of 100.4°F or higher. See when to worry by age, how to take your baby's temperature, which fever medicines are safe, home care tips, and when to call the doctor or go to the ER.
articles.title: Baby Fever: When to Worry and What to Do

articles.summary: Is it safe for babies to sleep on their stomach? Pediatricians recommend back sleeping for every sleep until age 1 to lower the risk of SIDS. Once your baby can roll both ways on their own, they can stay in the position they choose. Learn the AAP safe sleep guidelines, when stomach sleeping becomes safe, and how to set up a safe sleep space.
articles.title: Baby Sleeping on Stomach: Is It Safe? A Pediatrician Explains

articles.summary: Most short falls don't cause serious harm. A pediatrician walks you through the immediate red flags, the 24-hour warning signs, when to call 911 vs. your pediatrician vs. wait at home, and whether it's safe to let your baby sleep.
articles.title: My Baby Fell Off The Bed: What To Do (Pediatrician)
